fields.description:
Refuse a ticket at intake when its repository has no project checks entry and the source-control backend requires CI, instead of skipping the checks and denying the pull request at the promotion policy.

`config/local/checks.yaml.example` says a repository with no entry skips the checks gate with a warning. `run_checks` in `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/checks.py` returns `ran=False` for such a repository and `_ci_and_repair` in `services/orchestration/temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py` records `CHECKS_SKIPPED` and reports `CI_PASSED` with `ci_status="skipped"`. The run then pays for the code-review, security-review, and acceptance gates. `config/policies/promotion.rego` requires `ci_status == "success"` whenever `ci_required` holds, and `services/integration/opa/mediator.py` sets `ci_required` for the GitHub backend, so the skip can never pass there. The run is denied as `ci_not_successful`, the same reason a failing check produces.

Execution `intake-55f8b3f6` for rebar ticket `ff34-7786-fef6-4252` on `archive-massgov-pfml` spent about thirteen minutes in planning, implementation, and three review gates before that denial, because the operator file had lost its `archive-massgov-pfml` entry.

When the backend requires CI and the resolved repository has no checks entry, hold the ticket at intake with the reason `checks_not_configured` and alert, so no model spend happens. Record the ticket as deferred as well, because the fix lands in operator config rather than the ticket, and a rebar watermark poll would otherwise not read the ticket again until it changed. `required_checks_repos` in `services/orchestration/checks/config.py` resolves the configured repositories, or none when the backend does not require CI, and the contexts built by `reconcile_intake`, `_reconcile_rebar_pass` in `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/intake.py`, and `build_intake_context` in `services/orchestration/intake_runtime.py` carry its result in `IntakeContext.checks_repos`. A context built without it applies no check. Give the promotion policy a distinct `ci_skipped` reason for a skipped status, and narrow `ci_not_successful` to statuses other than success and skipped, so a run that reaches the policy another way reports the cause once. Update the template comment to state that the GitHub backend refuses a repository without an entry. The local backend, which does not require CI, keeps the current skip.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Intake holds a ticket for a later pass when its repository has no checks entry under the GitHub backend, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_reconciler.py -k holds_a_repository_without_checks_when_ci_is_required`
- [ ] Intake starts a ticket whose repository has no checks entry under the local backend, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_reconciler.py -k starts_a_repository_without_checks_when_ci_is_not_required`
- [ ] Intake starts a ticket whose repository has a checks entry under the GitHub backend, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_reconciler.py -k starts_a_repository_with_checks_when_ci_is_required`
- [ ] The configured repositories resolve under the GitHub backend, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_reconciler.py -k required_checks_repos_lists_configured_repositories_under_github`
- [ ] The promotion policy reports `ci_skipped` for a skipped status, proven by `pytest tests/integration/test_promotion_policy_rego.py -k skipped_ci_reports_ci_skipped`

## Testing
Run each acceptance criterion selector on its own with `python -m pytest`, which imports the checkout under test rather than the editable install. Run `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/inv ci` before closing the ticket.
